analysis: Both supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (lines 610-1755). The only reported change is in the head (lines ~3140-3240), which is outside the supplied text. The excerpt shows two new tests (remembersHeaderVerdictsOnlyForUnchangedFiles and replacedLookalikeIsReadAgain) for SSDWholeRootMaintainer. They check that a remembered header verdict is invalidated when the file's status-change time changes, even with size and mtime restored, and that a lookalike replaced by a real block is re-read. This is test-only code that tightens ownership proof for whole-root maintenance (TTL/LRU deletion), which is relevant to T-041 mitigation (b) and to the symlink and no-follow deletion safety shown in the base tests (lines 1544-1654). The patch excerpt is truncated and the production change that these tests exercise (SSDWholeRootMaintainer verdict caching) is not supplied. I could not confirm the maintainer's ctime and inode handling or the fail-safe behavior of deletion. No concrete regression is visible in the supplied evidence. The base text I reviewed contains existing tests on epoch preservation, TTL/sweep, write caps, and symlink handling, with nothing changed there. Open question for integration: verify that the production SSDWholeRootMaintainer change (not visible here) keys verdict memoization on ctime, inode, size and mtime, and never deletes files outside the owned DBK3 format. TTL cap 1800s and default-on gating are unchanged in the visible tests.
